name: Perth Hall
summary: Two six-storey residence wings combine smooth scored buff walls, split-face bays, white-framed paired casements, and sage spandrels. A raised central roof and a lower west service volume adjoin the residential wings.

evidence.note: The road-facing upper floors alternate recessed square windows and projecting three-sided window bays.
The east face shows coursed pale masonry extending down to the grass verge.
Beyond the low western service roof, window stacks alternate with broad light masonry panels.
The street facade close-up shows alternating textured rusticated courses, smooth buff piers, and slender silver mullions. The pale wall colour was sampled in sunlight.
The ground-level courtyard has full-height glazing and a recessed entrance behind a thin projecting canopy.
The long Western Road wing and offset west wing meet at a short raised link. A broad low roof adjoins the west wall. The two ends carry small rooftop equipment.
Inventory P50 / P90 / maximum: 18.92 / 21.52 / 26.08 m above local ground.

notes: Projecting window bays alternate between smooth stone faces and glass corner units. The west low roof is a double-height volume. The entry bay and secondary service door positions are approximate.
